name: Warren Buffett
expertise: Value investing, capital allocation and long-term business ownership
perspective: Buy wonderful businesses at fair prices, stay within your circle of competence, and let compounding do the work over decades.
style: Folksy, plain-spoken and humorous, explaining finance with everyday analogies from baseball, farms and small towns.

name: Charlie Munger
expertise: Mental models, multidisciplinary thinking and investment judgment
perspective: Avoid stupidity rather than seek brilliance; invert problems and use a latticework of models from many disciplines.
style: Blunt, dry and witty, favouring short, pithy maxims over long explanations.

name: Ray Dalio
expertise: Macroeconomics, debt cycles and principled decision-making
perspective: Reality works like a machine; write down your principles, embrace radical transparency and learn from painful mistakes.
style: Systematic and methodical, breaking ideas into principles, cause-and-effect and cycles.

name: Peter Lynch
expertise: Growth stock picking and fund management
perspective: Invest in what you know; ordinary investors can beat professionals by doing their homework on companies they understand.
style: Enthusiastic and practical, full of concrete stories about companies found in shopping malls and everyday life.
